questions.q: In the Northwind Retail capstone, what does "data currently on-premises" translate to technically?
options: Needing a self-hosted integration runtime to bridge on-prem SQL Server into Azure
Nothing — on-premises data can't be used with Data Factory at all
A requirement to physically move the SQL Server into Azure first
Using only the Azure integration runtime
questions.explain: Since the Azure IR can't reach a network it isn't in, on-premises data specifically requires a self-hosted integration runtime, covered in Chapter 7.

questions.q: Which course concept satisfies the requirement "no passwords sitting around in plain text"?
options: Managed identity and Key Vault-backed secrets
Writing passwords directly into the pipeline JSON
Storing credentials in a text file in the Git repo
This requirement can't actually be satisfied by Data Factory
questions.explain: Managed identities and Key Vault-referenced secrets, from Chapter 10, eliminate stored plain-text credentials entirely.

questions.q: Why does the lesson emphasize that requirements arrive as plain business language, not technical specs?
options: Because translating business language into an actual architecture is the real skill being tested
Because business language is always wrong and should be ignored
Because a real project never has any stakeholders
Because technical specs are always provided upfront in real jobs
questions.explain: Real-world requirements almost never arrive as "build a pipeline with X activity" — translating plain language into a concrete design is the actual work of a data engineer.

questions.q: In the end-to-end architecture diagram, what sits between the Copy activity's output and the final curated table?
options: A mapping data flow performing filter, derived column, aggregate, and join transformations
Nothing — the Copy activity writes directly to the curated table
A second, identical Copy activity
A Databricks notebook
questions.explain: The raw data landed by the Copy activity in ADLS Gen2 is transformed by a mapping data flow before landing in the curated Azure SQL Database table.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what does "done" for the capstone actually require, beyond the pipeline just running once successfully?
options: Handling failures gracefully, running unattended on schedule, being secured, and being explainable to someone else
Nothing more — a single successful manual run is sufficient to call it done
Only that the numbers in the final table are technically present, regardless of correctness
Passing a formal certification exam
questions.explain: The lesson's concrete finish line spans error handling, correct transformation logic, unattended scheduled execution, security, observability, and the ability to explain it clearly — not just a single working run.
